title: Aortic regurgitation and root disease: pathophysiology, Bentall and David procedures

steps.say: Chronic aortic regurgitation imposes combined volume and pressure overload on the left ventricle. In response to massive regurgitant flow, the myocardium develops eccentric hypertrophy and progressive cavity dilatation. This chamber remodeling preserves forward stroke volume for years before systolic function declines.
steps.tx: Chronic aortic regurgitation imposes severe diastolic **volume overload** on the left ventricle, provoking progressive **eccentric hypertrophy** and marked chamber enlargement. The ventricle dilates to accommodate a massive **total stroke volume**, preserving effective forward systemic cardiac output until myocardial contractility ultimately decompensates.

steps.say: Echocardiography establishes the severity of chronic regurgitation using standardized quantitative criteria. Severe regurgitation is defined by a regurgitant volume of 60 millilitres or greater and a regurgitant fraction of 50 percent or greater. A vena contracta width exceeding 6 millimetres confirms severe incompetence.
steps.tx: Quantitative echocardiography defines severe regurgitation by a **regurgitant volume** of 60 mL or greater, a **regurgitant fraction** of 50 percent or higher, an effective regurgitant orifice of 0.30 cm2 or greater, and a **vena contracta** width exceeding 6 mm on color Doppler imaging.

steps.say: Surgical intervention is indicated in asymptomatic patients before irreversible ventricular failure develops. An ejection fraction of 55 percent or lower or an end-systolic dimension exceeding 50 millimetres mandates surgical repair or replacement. Operating at these thresholds preserves postoperative ventricular recovery.
steps.tx: Surgery is indicated in **asymptomatic AR** when resting left ventricular **ejection fraction** falls to 55 percent or lower, or when the left ventricular **end-systolic dimension** exceeds 50 mm (or indexed dimension exceeds 25 mm/m2), preventing irreversible cardiomyocyte apoptosis and postoperative heart failure.

nodes.label: Severe chronic aortic regurgitation confirmed on echo
Assess symptoms: dyspnea, angina, or heart failure
Asymptomatic: check LVEF <= 55% or LVESD > 50 mm
Proceed with elective aortic valve or root surgery

steps.say: Acute aortic regurgitation presents very differently from chronic regurgitation. Massive retrograde flow enters a small, non-compliant ventricle, causing sudden end-diastolic pressure elevation. This causes premature mitral valve closure and rapid cardiovascular collapse requiring emergency surgery.
steps.tx: In **acute aortic regurgitation** from dissection or endocarditis, sudden regurgitant volume floods a stiff, non-compliant chamber. Left ventricular diastolic pressure rises precipitously, causing **premature mitral valve closure** and acute pulmonary edema, culminating in catastrophic **cardiovascular collapse** that demands emergency surgical intervention.

left.title: Acute Aortic Regurgitation
points: Extremely high left ventricular end-diastolic pressure
Premature mitral closure and rapid pulmonary edema

right.title: Chronic Aortic Regurgitation
points: Massively dilated left ventricle with eccentric hypertrophy
Normal or compensated resting diastolic pressure
Widened pulse pressure with bounding peripheral pulses

steps.say: The Bentall procedure replaces the aortic valve, aortic root, and ascending aorta with a composite valved conduit. Coronary artery ostia are excised as circular buttons and reimplanted directly into the graft. This modified button Bentall technique remains the standard for annuloaortic ectasia.
steps.tx: The modified button **Bentall procedure** replaces the diseased valve, aortic sinuses, and ascending aorta using a **composite valved conduit**. The coronary ostia are mobilized as circular **coronary buttons** and reimplanted directly into the neo-aortic Dacron tube graft, achieving reliable hemostasis and anatomical reconstruction.

nodes.label: Resect diseased aortic root and excise coronary buttons
Suture composite valved conduit to aortic annulus
Reimplant left and right coronary buttons into Dacron tube
Construct distal ascending aortic end-to-end anastomosis

steps.say: Valve-sparing root replacement preserves healthy native aortic leaflets inside a Dacron graft. The David reimplantation procedure anchors the aortic annulus inside the prosthetic cylinder, stabilizing both the annulus and the sinotubular junction. This avoids lifelong anticoagulation in young patients.
steps.tx: The **David procedure** achieves **valve-sparing root replacement** using a circumferential **reimplantation technique**. The intact native valve leaflets are suspended inside a Dacron graft, stabilizing the dilated annulus and sinotubular junction while preserving physiological cusp motion and completely eliminating lifelong anticoagulation in young patients.

left.title: David Reimplantation Procedure
points: Places Dacron tube graft outside aortic annulus
Provides rigid subannular and sinotubular stabilization
Optimal long-term freedom from recurrent regurgitation

right.title: Yacoub Remodeling Procedure
points: Sutures scalloped Dacron graft to aortic sinuses
Preserves physiological root expansion during systole
No subannular ring; higher late failure in annular ectasia

steps.say: The Yacoub remodeling technique replaces the three aortic sinuses with a scalloped Dacron graft without annular fixation. While it preserves dynamic root motion during the cardiac cycle, lack of subannular stabilization leads to late recurrent regurgitation in extensive annuloaortic ectasia.
steps.tx: The **Yacoub technique** employs a scalloped Dacron prosthesis to reconstruct the sinuses of Valsalva using an anatomical **remodeling technique**. Because it lacks formal subannular ring stabilization, it carries higher rates of late failure when performed in patients with severe **annuloaortic ectasia**.

steps.say: Aortic valve repair requires precise intraoperative leaflet assessment. Measure geometric leaflet height, which normally ranges between 9 and 10 millimetres, and achieve an effective coaptation height greater than 9 millimetres. Central leaflet plication corrects prolapse and restores durable valve competence.
steps.tx: Aortic valve repair demands precise intraoperative measurement of **geometric height** (normal 9 to 10 mm) and restoration of an **effective coaptation height** greater than 9 mm above the annular plane. Cusp prolapse is corrected with central **leaflet plication** or free-margin resuspension.
